# Volume 1 — CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Properly Horrified

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

TWO weeks had passed while NELL stayed at Grey Shutters prior to Mrs. Sowerby's arrival to check on her. Mrs. Agatha was not at fault for this, if one is to be fair to her. Ever since the time she had last visited Grey Shutters, a harsh and untimely bout of influenza had kept that fine woman indoors. Illness rarely struck Mrs. Agatha, and she held a distinct disdain for those whom it affected; yet, she declared, influenza resembled no other ailment in existence and was best understood as a peculiar trial sent by Providence. The moment her physician permitted her to step outside, she rushed to Grey Shutters, consumed by an eager desire to view Obed and Thirza’s orphan, about whom many rumors and conjectures had circulated throughout Brierley.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0000 }

Nell had utilized all her conscious time during those two weeks productively. Every single tree and bush around the property was already familiar to her. She had found a lane that began under the apple orchard and extended upward through a strip of woods; moreover, she had traversed it to its absolute terminus across all its delightful variations of stream and bridge, fir grove and wild cherry canopy, nooks dense with ferns, and splitting paths of maple and rowan.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0001 }

A friendship had been formed by her with the spring located down in the hollow—that marvellous, profound, transparent, freezing spring; smooth red sandstones surrounded it, and huge clumps of water fern resembling palms bordered it; furthermore, a log bridge spanned the brook past that point.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0002 }

That bridge conducted Nell’s dancing feet up across a wooded hill past it, where an unending twilight prevailed beneath the erect, densely packed firs and spruces; the sole flowers in that place were countless fragile “June bells,” those shyest and sweetest of forest blooms, and several pale, high-born starflowers, resembling the ghosts of last year’s blossoms. Cobwebs shone like silver threads in the midst of the trees and the fir boughs and tassels appeared to speak kindly words.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0003 }

Every one of these ecstatic journeys of discovery occurred during the brief half-hour breaks granted to her for recreation, and Nell babbled to Obed and Thirza until they were nearly deafened by her findings. Not that Obed ever voiced a grievance, naturally; he took in every detail with a mute, pleased grin upon his countenance; Thirza endured the “chatter” right up to the moment she realized it was capturing her attention too deeply, at which point she invariably silenced Nell at once with a sharp order to keep quiet.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0004 }

Nell was in the orchard while Mrs. Agatha arrived, strolling wherever she pleased amid the deep, quivering grasses flecked with reddish twilight sunlight; thus, that kindly woman possessed a great opportunity to thoroughly discuss her sickness, detailing each pain and throbbing heart-rate with such clear pleasure that Thirza concluded that even grippe had to offer its rewards. Once the specifics were finished, Mrs. Agatha presented the actual motive for her visit.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0005 }

“Certain astonishing reports regarding you and Obed have reached my ears.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0006 }

“I reckon you are just as astonished as I am,” Thirza remarked. “My own astonishment is starting to fade now.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0007 }

“It was a shame that such an error occurred,” Mrs. Agatha remarked with sympathy. “Were you unable to return her?”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0008 }

“It would be possible, I imagine, yet our decision was otherwise. Obed developed a liking for her. Furthermore, I have to agree that I am fond of her as well—even though her flaws are apparent to me. Already, the atmosphere of the house feels changed. A truly intelligent young lady, that is what she is.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0009 }

Because she perceived condemnation upon Mrs. Agatha’s countenance, Thirza uttered a greater amount than she had planned upon starting.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0010 }

“You have assumed a heavy burden,” that lady remarked somberly, “particularly since you possess no prior background with young ones. I imagine you are largely unfamiliar with her and her true character, and it is impossible to predict how a youth of that nature will develop. However, Thirza, I certainly do not intend to dishearten you.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0011 }

“I’m not feeling discouraged,” Thirza answered dryly, “when my mind is made up to do something, it remains made up. I imagine you’d want to see Nell. I will bring her inside.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0012 }

Nell came darting inside shortly, her visage gleaming with the joy of her wanderings through the orchard; however, embarrassed to discover herself in the unpredicted company of a unknown person, she stopped in confusion just within the doorway. She was undeniably a strange-appearing small being in the cropped, fitted wincey garment she had carried from the asylum, beneath which her slender legs appeared clumsily elongated. Her freckles were increasingly plentiful and noticeable than before; the breeze had whipped her bare hair into a excessively bright mess; it had at no time appeared more fiery than right then.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0013 }

“Well, they didn’t choose you on account of your appearance, that’s without a doubt,” Mrs. Agatha Sowerby remarked emphatically. Mrs. Agatha belonged to that charming and well-liked group of individuals who take pride in voicing their opinions without dread or partiality. “She’s awfully thin and plain, Thirza. Step over this way, child, so I can inspect you. Goodness gracious, has anyone ever witnessed such freckles? And hair that is as red as carrots! Step over this way, child, I tell you.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0014 }

Nell “came there,” though not quite in the manner Mrs. Agatha anticipated. Crossing the kitchen floor in a single leap, she halted in front of Mrs. Agatha, her visage crimson with fury, her lips shaking, and her entire slight frame quivering top to bottom.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0015 }

“My hatred for you is absolute,” she wept with a strangled tone, bringing her foot down hard against the ground. “My hatred for you—my hatred for you—my hatred for you—” with every declaration of her intense dislike, her foot struck the ground even more forcefully. “What gives you the right to describe me as scrawny and unattractive? What gives you the right to claim that I have freckles and red hair? Your behavior is that of a crude, ill-mannered, heartless female!”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0016 }

“Nell!” Thirza cried out, alarmed.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0017 }

Yet Nell stayed confronting Mrs. Agatha fearlessly, her head raised, her eyes burning, her hands balled into fists, as a fervent rage radiated off her like an aura.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0018 }

“How dare you make those statements regarding me?” she demanded with great force. “How would it feel if those statements were made regarding you? How would it feel to be informed that you are heavy and awkward and likely lacked a single bit of imagination? It matters nothing to me if my saying so hurts your feelings! My wish is to hurt them. You have injured my feelings more deeply than they have ever been injured previously, even by Mrs. Thomas’ intoxicated husband. And my forgiveness will never be given to you for it, never, never!”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0019 }

Thump! Thump!
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0020 }

“Was such a temper ever witnessed by anyone!” cried the appalled Mrs. Agatha.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0021 }

“Nell, head to your chamber and remain there till I join you,” Thirza said, barely regaining her ability to talk.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0022 }

Dissolving into tears, Nell hurried toward the door to the hall, shutting it with enough force to cause the tins hanging on the exterior porch wall to rattle along, before she sped through the hallway and ascended the staircase with the speed of a whirlwind. A muffled bang from the upper floor indicated that she had closed the east gable door with just as much fury.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0023 }

“Indeed, I do not envy the task you have in raising that child, Thirza,” Mrs. Agatha stated with profound gravity.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0024 }

Thirza parted her lips, intending to speak some unknown words of excuse or regret. The actual statement that left her mouth astonished her at that moment and continuously throughout the rest of her life.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0025 }

“Agatha, it was wrong of you to mock her appearance.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0026 }

“Thirza Abernethy, are you actually suggesting that you support her after the appalling fit of rage we just witnessed?” Mrs. Agatha asked with indignation.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0027 }

“No,” Thirza said unhurriedly, “excusing her is not my intention. Her behavior has been quite bad, so a scolding from me is necessary. However, we have to consider her background. Nobody ever instructed her on proper conduct. Furthermore, your treatment of her was overly harsh, Agatha.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0028 }

Thirza was unable to refrain from appending that final remark, even though her own actions once more astonished her. Rising, Mrs. Agatha assumed a posture of wounded pride.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0029 }

“Indeed, Thirza, it is clear to me now that my future words must be chosen with extreme caution, given that the sensitive emotions of parentless children, fetched from who knows where, now take precedence over all other matters. No, indeed, I am not offended—there is no need to trouble yourself. My sympathy for you is so great that it leaves no space in my thoughts for wrath. That youngster will surely cause you no end of grief. However, if you are willing to accept my counsel—which I imagine you will ignore, despite my having raised ten boys and girls and laid two in the ground—the ‘talking to’ you spoke of ought to be delivered using a reasonably large birch rod. In my opinion, that sort of child understands that type of speech best. It seems to me that her fiery mood corresponds with the color of her hair. Anyway, good night, Thirza. It is my hope that you will continue to drop by my place frequently as you always have. Nevertheless, you must not anticipate my coming back to this home anytime soon, provided I am at risk of being pounced upon and demeaned in this manner. Nothing like this has ever occurred in my life before.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0030 }

At this, Mrs. Agatha departed—assuming a stout female whose gait was a perpetual waddle could be described as departing—while Thirza, bearing a exceedingly grave expression, directed her steps toward the east gable.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0031 }

As she went up the stairs, she mused with apprehension about the proper course of action. The incident that had just taken place filled her with considerable dismay. It was so unlucky that Nell had exhibited such an ill humor in front of Mrs. Agatha Sowerby, above everyone else! At that moment, Thirza was abruptly struck by a disturbing and accusatory awareness that this caused her greater shame than grief over revealing so grave a flaw in Nell’s character. Furthermore, in what manner should she discipline her? The gentle recommendation regarding the birch switch—whose effectiveness could be painfully attested to by every one of Mrs. Agatha’s own offspring—held no attraction for Thirza. She doubted her ability to flog a child. Instead, a different form of chastisement had to be devised to make Nell adequately comprehend the magnitude of her wrongdoing.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0032 }

Thirza discovered Nell weeping disconsolately while lying face down upon her bed, completely unmindful of the dirt from her boots soiling a spotless counterpane.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0033 }

“Nell,” she uttered with a degree of softness.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0034 }

There was no reply.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0035 }

“Nell,” with increased sternness, “get off that bed right now and pay attention to my words to you.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0036 }

Nell wriggled down from the bed and took a stiff seat on an adjacent chair, her puffy face marked by tears while her gaze remained obstinately attached to the ground.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0037 }

“You are acting in a fine manner, Nell! Do you not feel shame?”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0038 }

“She lacked the right to call me redheaded and ugly,” Nell replied, avoiding the point and acting defensively.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0039 }

“You were not entitled to become so enraged and speak in that manner to her, Nell. My shame regarding you was complete—utterly complete. My desire was for you to act courteously toward Mrs. Sowerby, yet you brought shame upon me rather than doing so. It is quite beyond me why Mrs. Sowerby mentioning that you possess red hair and plain looks should cause you to fly into a rage like that. You state the very same thing frequently yourself.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0040 }

“Oh, but saying something yourself is so completely different from hearing someone else say it,” Nell cried out. “A thing might be known to you as fact, yet you cannot stop hoping that others do not entirely believe it to be so. It must seem to you that my temper is terrible, but it was beyond my control. When those words came from her, something simply swelled up inside me and suffocated me. I was forced to lash out at her.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0041 }

“Indeed, you displayed yourself in a splendid manner, I am bound to remark. A delightful tale concerning you will be spread far and wide by Mrs. Sowerby—and without doubt, she will share it. For you to become so enraged was a terrible occurrence, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0042 }

“Try to picture what your reactions would be if a person stated directly to you that you were scrawny and hideous,” begged Nell through her tears.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0043 }

A former memory unexpectedly occurred to Thirza. Having been a tiny child, she had overheard one aunt remark about her to another aunt, “What a pity she is such a dark, homely little thing.” Thirza reached fully fifty years of age before that recollection ceased to cause her pain.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0044 }

“Nell, I am not claiming I believe Mrs. Sowerby acted entirely properly when she spoke to you in that manner,” she conceded with less harshness in her voice. “Agatha speaks her mind too freely. However, that does not justify you acting as you did. Being an unfamiliar face, an aged lady, and a guest in my home are three separate, compelling grounds for you to have shown her deference. Your conduct was disrespectful and impudent, and”—a fortunate idea for a penalty struck Thirza—“you are required to approach her, express deep regret for losing your cool, and beg for her pardon.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0045 }

“That is something I will never do,” declared Nell with dark resolve. “You are free to penalize me however you wish, Thirza. You may lock me away inside a pitch-black, soggy vault filled with serpents and amphibians while giving me nothing to eat but bread and water, and no protest will come from me. However, I am incapable of begging Mrs. Sowerby for her pardon.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0046 }

“It is not our practice to lock individuals inside cold wet vaults,” Thirza remarked crisply, “mainly because they are quite rare in Brierley. However, you are required to make amends to Mrs. Sowerby, and you will remain confined to this room until you are able to inform me of your readiness to comply.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0047 }

“Then this means I must remain here for all time,” Nell stated sorrowfully, “since apologizing to Mrs. Sowerby for what I uttered to her is impossible for me. In what way could I? Remorse is not what I feel. My regret lies in having upset you; nevertheless, delivering those exact words to her brought me joy. The feeling of relief was immense. Expressing regret when it does not exist is impossible for me, is it not? Conceiving that I am regretful is beyond my ability.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0048 }

“Maybe your morning state of mind will improve the functioning of your imagination,” Thirza remarked, getting up to leave. “The night lies ahead for you to ponder your behavior and attain a superior mental attitude. Your promise was to endeavor to be an exceptionally well-behaved girl should we retain you at Grey Shutters, yet I am bound to remark that tonight’s events have hardly reflected that.”
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0049 }

Abandoning this parting blow to fester within Nell’s tempestuous heart, Thirza went down into the kitchen, deeply disturbed in spirit and annoyed in her innermost self. Her irritation was directed as much at herself as at Nell, since, each time she remembered the speechlessly astonished face of Mrs. Agatha, her lips quivered with entertainment and she experienced a highly blameworthy impulse to chuckle.
{: #nw-v01-c09-p0050 }
